blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Learned lossless codecs make smaller files than common classical codecs, yet the images we archive and train on still use classical codecs. A main reason is time: a learned codec takes seconds to decode a photo that a classical codec opens in milliseconds, and their faster variants give up most of their gain in size. We argue that much of this time is spent waiting, not computing: the network waits for the values it conditions on, and the arithmetic decoder reads them one at a time. We introduce FMT (Fixed-step Multiscale Tree), a lossless image format whose decoding order and entropy coder are designed together so that neither wait grows with the image. FMT stores an image as a coarse-to-fine tree whose steps hold independent values: a GPU predicts each step at once and decodes it in parallel rANS lanes that carry their states from step to step, so an image of any size decodes in a fixed number of sequential steps. On this tree we build a family of bit-exact codecs, from a rule with no network to large networks, and no codec we ran on the same GPU beats any of them on both size and speed. Without a network, FMT beats NVIDIA's HTJ2K on size and speed; with a large one, it decodes Kodak photos 9 to 61X faster than learned codecs we ran on the same A100, at the same size or smaller.
blocks.zh: 所学的无损失解码器比普通的古典解码器要小,然而我们归档和训练的图像仍然使用古典解码器. 一个主要原因是时间:一个被学习的解码器需要几秒钟才能解码出一个以毫秒为单位打开的古典解码器相片,而他们的更快的变体放弃了大部分的大小收益. 我们争论说,这大部分时间都是在等待,而不是计算:网络在等待它所附带的值,算术解码器一次读一次. 我们引入了FMT(Fixed-step-Multiscale Tree),这是一种无损失的图像格式,其解码顺序和 en码器是一起设计的,这样两个等都无法与图像一起生长. blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Many images must be stored without losing a single pixel: originals in archives, frames in editing pipelines, and the training data of models that restore images. Such images are written once and read many times, so how fast they decode matters as much as how small they are. Classical lossless codecs, such as PNG, JPEG-LS, JPEG XL and HTJ2K, predict or transform pixels with hand-designed rules [ 63 , 60 , 11 , 2 , 51 ] and decode a photo in milliseconds. Learned codecs replace these rules with neural networks and make clearly smaller files [ 33 , 4 , 69 , 28 , 27 ] , but they take seconds per photo, tens to hundreds of times longer ( Fig. 4 ), and their faster designs give up most of the gain in size [ 28 , 23 ] . One must still choose between size and speed.
blocks.zh: 许多图像必须在不丢失单一像素的情况下被存储:原始的档案,编辑管道的帧,以及恢复图像的模型的培训数据. 这类图像被写出一次并读出多遍,所以它们解码的速度和大小一样重要. 经典的无损解码器,如PNG,JPEG-LS,JPEG XL和HTJ2K,用手设计的规则预测或转换像素[63,60,11,2,51],并用毫秒来解码一张照片. 所学的编解码器用神经网络来取而代之,并制作出明显更小的文件[33,4,69,28,27],但它们每张照片需要几秒钟,长了几十到几百倍(图4),它们更快的设计放弃了大部分的大小收益[28,23]. 人们仍然必须在大小和速度之间作出选择。

blocks.en: Why are learned codecs so slow? We argue that much of their time goes to waiting rather than computing ( Tab. 1 ). An entropy decoder can recover a value only once it knows the value’s probability, and a learned codec computes it from values decoded before it. Decoding is therefore a chain with two links. First, the network waits for the values it conditions on: once per value in a pixel-by-pixel model [ 56 ] , and still many times in codecs that predict groups of values [ 41 , 8 , 43 , 22 , 28 ] . Second, the arithmetic decoder reads one value after another, often on the CPU. FNLIC [ 68 ] reports 13 ms of network inference per photo, yet in our runs it took half a second per photo, two fifths of it in such a coder; LC-FDNet [ 43 ] took a second, a fifth of it in its coder on the CPU. No number of GPU cores shortens this chain ( a).
blocks.zh: 为什么学习的解码器这么慢? 我们争辩说,他们的大部分时间是等待而不是计算(Tab. 1)。 一个等效解码器只有在知道该值的概率后才能恢复一个值,而一个已学习的解码器从它之前的解码值中计算出来. 因此,解码是一个链条,有两个链接。 首先,网络等待它所条件的值:在像素逐像素模型中每值一次[56],在预测值组的编码器中仍然有多次[41,8,43,22,28]. 第二,算术解码器读取一个又一个值,常在CPU上. LC-FDNet[43]在CPU的编码器中用了1秒钟,其中五分之一。 没有GPU核数缩短了这个链 (a).

blocks.en: In FMT, every pixel is the end of a path from a coarse root ( b), as every weight is in state trees [ 3 ] : each level adds the pixels halfway between those already decoded, predicts them from their decoded neighbours and stores only a correction (the residual), so neighbouring pixels share the top of their paths, the coarser pixels they are predicted from. Each correction is in turn binarised into a short path of decisions: its size, then its bits.
blocks.zh: 在FMT中,每个像素都是从粗细根(b)出道的终点,因为每个重量都在州立树上[3]: 每个关卡在已经解码的中间添加了像素,从被解码的邻居那里预测它们,并且只存储一个校正(剩余),因此相邻的像素共享其路径的顶端,相邻的像素是它们预言的相干像素. 每个更正又被二进制成一个简短的决定路径:大小,然后是位数。

blocks.en: This tree is what lets the decoder run in parallel. A pixel depends only on pixels of earlier steps, so the values of one step do not depend on each other: the GPU predicts them all at once, and interleaved streams of rANS [ 12 , 14 ] , a fast entropy coder, which we call lanes, decode their corrections in parallel, each lane carrying its state from one step to the next. Coarse-to-fine orders have long been used in image coding [ 44 , 25 , 22 ] ; what we add is an entropy coder designed together with the order, with lanes sized by the image, not by the step as in vectorised ANS [ 55 ] , so that neither link of the chain grows with the image. Since the root’s spacing is fixed in pixels, a photo of any size decodes in at most 72 steps, and no lane decodes more than a set number of values ( Tab. 1 ): the depth is fixed, though a larger photo has larger steps.
blocks.zh: 这棵树让解码器平行运行. 一个像素只依赖于早期步骤的像素,所以一个步骤的值并不互相依赖:GPU一次全部预测,并互出流出rANS [12,14],一个快的 en码器,我们称之为道,平行地解码他们的校正,每个道将它的状态从一步传到下一步. 粗到细的指令早就被用在了图像编码上 [44, 25, 22];我们所添加的是一个与顺序一起设计的 en码器,由图像大小的车道,而不是向量化的ANS [55]中的步骤,这样链条的链条都无法与图像相接而长出. 由于根的相距以像素固定,所以任意大小相片在最多72个步中解码,没有道道解码超过设定数值(Tab. 1):深度是固定的,尽管更大的相片有更大的相片步.

blocks.en: The tree also hosts classical and learned lossless coding in one format. It fixes which values are decoded together, but not how each is predicted or how its path is paid for, so hand-designed rules and neural networks become modes of the same format: a fast mode stores the corrections of a reversible wavelet at fixed widths, with no entropy coder; a dense mode predicts each pixel by the mean of four neighbours and codes the paths with histograms learned once, with no network; and neural modes, with networks from 16 neurons in 2 layers (16 × \times 2) to 768 in 4 (768 × \times 4), give every possible correction its own probability, and the encoder tunes them to each photo. All decode bit-exactly on the GPU, and on other GPU types with our portable kernels.
blocks.zh: 该树还以一种格式主持古典和所学的无损失编码. 它固定了哪些值是一起解码的,但没有确定每个值是如何预测的,或者如何支付路径的,所以手工设计的规则和神经网络成为同一格式的模式:一个快模式将可逆波的校正以固定的宽度存储,没有正弦编码器;一个密集模式以四个邻居的平均值来预测每个像素,并且用一次学习到的直径图的路径编码,没有网络;神经模式,网络从2层的16个神经元(16××时2分)到4个(768×时4分)的768个神经元,给予每一个可能的校正概率,编码器将其调和每个相片. 在GPU上全部解码比特精确,在其他GPU类型上则使用我们的可移植内核.

blocks.en: Across this family, no codec we ran on the same GPU beats any FMT mode on both size and speed, on Kodak or on two sets of large photos ( Figs. 4 and 3 ). Without a network, FMT beats NVIDIA’s HTJ2K in both size and speed. With a small network, it makes smaller files than JPEG XL and decodes them faster on one GPU than JPEG XL does on a 32-thread CPU. With a large network, it decodes a Kodak photo 9 to 61 × \times faster than the learned codecs we ran from their authors’ code on an A100, at the same size or smaller ( Tab. 4 ). At full load, the fast mode decodes more pixels per second than any other codec we ran ( Tab. 6 ).
blocks.zh: 在柯达克或两套相片(图4和图3)上, 没有网络,FMT在大小和速度上都击败了NVIDIA的HTJ2K. 通过一个小的网络,它使文件比JPEG XL更小,并在一个GPU上解码它们的速度比JPEG XL在一个32行的CPU上解码的速度快. 使用大型网络,它解码出一张柯达克相片9至61xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx 在满载时,快模式解码的像素每秒比我们运行的任何其他编码器(Tab. 6)多.

blocks.en: In summary, we make three contributions: 1. Where the time of learned lossless decoding goes. Profiles of three released codecs, and our own networks decoded with longer coder chains or more steps, show that much of it goes to waiting, not computing ( Sec. 4.4 , Sec. S6.6). 2. A decoding schedule whose sequential work does not grow with the image. The order and the entropy coder are designed together: a coarse-to-fine tree of corrections, each a short path of decisions, fixes the number of steps by its root’s spacing, and rANS lanes whose number grows with the image carry their states across steps, so prediction and entropy decoding both run in parallel on the GPU. Neither half suffices alone: with one coder, the same order still takes most of a second [ 22 ] ; with fresh lanes at every step, files grow by up to 14% (about 24% in the dense mode; Secs. 3.1 , 3.2 , 3.4 and 3.5 , Sec. S3.3). 3. Bit-exact codecs, measured end to end. GPU decoders for every mode, portable kernels whose streams decode alike on different GPUs (also with 8-bit tensor-core layers) and CPU decoders, compared from compressed bytes to verified pixels with classical codecs on one GPU and one CPU and with learned codecs run from their authors’ code, including where they still win ( Secs. 4 and 5 ).

S6.6. 2. 编解码时间表,其相继工作不随图像而增长. 顺序和等效编码器是一起设计的:一棵粗细至细的校正树,每条短道决定,按根相间隔来固定步数,而数字随图像而增长的RANS道则会携带其状态跨出步数,因此预测和等效解码在GPU上平行运行. 仅凭两个半就够了:只要有一个编码器,同样的顺序仍然需要大部分秒 [22];只要每一步都有新鲜的车道,文件就会增长多达14%(在密集模式中约为24%;第3.1、3.2、3.4和3.5条,第S3.3条)。 3. Bit-exact 解码器,被测量到端. 每种模式的GPU解码器,可移植的内核,其流在不同GPU上同样解码(也带有8位的收分-收分层)和CPU解码器,从压缩字节到在一个GPU和一个CPU上用古典解码器验证的像素,以及从作者代码上运行的已学习的解码器,包括它们仍然取胜的地方(secs. 4和5).

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Most lossless codecs predict each pixel from decoded neighbours and code the residual: CALIC [ 63 ] and LOCO-I, the core of JPEG-LS [ 60 ] , in raster order with fixed predictors and adaptive contexts; PNG [ 11 ] , WebP [ 64 ] and QOI [ 50 ] with simpler rules; FLIF [ 49 ] and JPEG XL [ 2 , 48 ] with a context tree learned for each image; GraLIC [ 42 ] mixes many predictors per pixel, far more slowly. JPEG 2000 [ 52 ] decorrelates the image with a reversible integer wavelet [ 7 ] , and HTJ2K [ 51 ] codes it with a high-throughput block coder. Coarse-to-fine orders are old: hierarchical interpolation [ 44 , 46 ] predicts from coarser grids, Kim and Cho [ 25 ] pair such a hierarchy with context-adaptive arithmetic coding, much as our dense mode does, and FLIF’s interlaced mode, PNG’s Adam7 [ 11 ] and JPEG XL’s Squeeze [ 48 ] decode coarse to fine.
blocks.zh: 大多数无损失的编码器从已解码的相邻处预测出每个像素,并编码了剩余部分:CALIC [63]和LOCO-I,JPEG-LS [60]的核心,以有固定预测器和适应环境的光栅顺序;PNG [11],WebP [64]和QOI [50],规则更简单;FLIF [49]和JPEG XL [2,48],每个图像都学了上下文树;GraLIC [42]每像素混合了许多预测器,速度更慢. JPEG 2000 [52]用可逆整数的波浪来装饰图像,而HTJ2K [51]用高通量块编码器来编码. 粗到细的指令是古老的:分级内插[44,46]从粗到细的网格上预测出,金和Cho[25]将这样的分级与上下文的算法编码成对,就像我们的稠密模式一样,FLIF的相接模式,PNG的Adam7[11]和JPEG XL的克塞[48]解码粗到细.

blocks.en: PixelCNN [ 56 , 47 ] runs a network per value. Later codecs predict groups of values: multi- and subscale models [ 41 , 32 , 65 ] , hierarchical latents (L3C [ 33 ] , SHVC [ 45 ] ), super-resolution (SReC [ 8 ] ), frequency bands (LC-FDNet [ 43 ] ), lossy plus residual (RC [ 34 ] , DLPR [ 4 ] ) and bit planes (ArIB-BPS [ 69 ] ). Integer flows [ 18 , 67 , 66 , 59 ] , probabilistic circuits [ 31 ] , per-image fitting (FNLIC [ 68 ] , and for lossy coding Cool-chic [ 26 ] and C3 [ 24 ] ) and adaptation ( CALLIC [ 27 ] ) differ; checkerboard contexts [ 17 , 16 ] decode lossy latents in two steps.
blocks.zh: PixelCNN [56,47] 运行一个网络每值. 后期编码器预测了数值的组别:多和分尺度模型[41,32,65],分级潜伏(L3C [33],SHVC [45]),超分辨率(SReC [8]),频带(LC-FDNet [43]),损失加剩余(RC [34],DLPR [4])和比特平面(ARIB-BPS [69]). 整流[18,67,66,59],概率电路 [31],活像相配(HULIC [68],并用于失序编码 Cool-chic [26]和C3 [24])和适应相配(CallIC [27])不同;跳板上下文 [17,16]分两步解码丢失潜伏.

blocks.en: The attempt most similar to FMT is Kamisli’s interpolation codec [ 22 ] , which stores a sparse grid of pixels and predicts the finer grids from coarser ones with small networks: essentially our decoding order. Its network runs only about 15 times per image, yet it still takes most of a second per photo by its paper, because a single arithmetic coder on the CPU decodes every value in turn. HPAC [ 28 ] bounds its network steps by working on patches and comes closest to our largest networks in size, but by its paper it takes about a second per Kodak photo, 17 times as long as our 512 × \times 4. PILC [ 23 ] takes the opposite route: it runs entirely on the GPU and is fast, but its files are about as large as WebP’s, which our dense mode, without any network, beats in both size and throughput ( Tab. 6 ). Wavefront codecs [ 6 , 15 ] decode many pixels at once, DLIC [ 6 ] with rANS on the GPU, but in steps whose number grows with the image ( Sec. 4.4 ). Together they show that a parallel order alone does not make decoding fast, and that speed bought with a simple model gives up the size. For lossy video, DCVC-RT [ 20 ] finds speed limited by operations other than computation and trims them in its network; FMT instead bounds the number of sequential steps. What FMT adds is an entropy coder designed together with its order: the values of each step are spread over interleaved rANS lanes that carry their states from step to step, and the predictors are cheap enough per step, with integer probabilities, to keep both prediction and entropy decoding on the GPU, bit-exact. Unlike JPEG XL and HTJ2K, which decode in parallel by coding blocks of the image apart, so that no value sees across a block’s border, FMT splits no image into blocks.
blocks.zh: 与FMT最相似的尝试是卡米斯利的插值编码克 [22],它存储了少量像素的网格并预测出由有小网络的相近网所形成的更细的网格:基本上是我们的解码顺序. 其网络每张相片运行约15次,然而每张相片仍需要用纸取出大部分秒数,因为CPU上的单个算术编码器依次解码出每个值. HPAC[28]通过补丁来限制其网络步骤,并且最接近我们最大的网络大小,但是通过它的纸张,每高达克相片需要一秒左右,长于我们的512×x\时长的17倍. 4. PILC [23] 采取相反的路线:它完全运行在GPU上,而且速度快,但其文件大约与WebP一样大,我们密集的模式,没有任何网络,在大小和吞吐量上都比得上(Tab. 6). 波前编码器 [6, 15] 一次解码出多个像素, DLIC [6] 有 RANS 在GPU上,但以其数随图像而增长的步数(sec 4.4). 它们共同表明,单靠一个平行的订单并不能使解码速度快,而用一个简单的模型购买的速度则放弃了尺寸. 对于丢失的视频,DCVC-RT [20]发现速度受到除计算以外的操作的限制,并会在其网络中进行修剪;而FMT则会限定相继步骤的数量. FMT所添加的是一个与它的顺序一起设计的 en编码器:每个步骤的值被分布在将状态从步到步相接的相接的rANS道上,而预测器每步足够便宜,有整数概率,可以保持GPU上的预测和 en解码,位-正. 与JPEG XL和HTJ2K不同的是,它们通过图像的编码块将图像相隔并列解码,这样没有值看到一个块的边框,FMT就没有将图像分割成块.

blocks.en: Classical formats already decode on GPUs: NVIDIA’s libraries decode JPEG 2000, HTJ2K [ 39 ] , TIFF [ 38 ] and general-purpose formats [ 37 ] . Huffman [ 61 ] and ANS [ 12 , 62 , 30 , 21 ] streams decode in parallel once split into parts or interleaved [ 14 ] , and vectorised ANS brings this to learned codecs [ 55 ] . These methods parallelise the coder once the probabilities of many values are known; in a learned codec, the decoding order decides how many are known at once, and the tree of FMT makes them every value of a step. As in vectorised ANS, our lanes keep their states across stages, but their number follows the image, not the step, so steps of 96 to 98,304 values share them ( Sec. 3.4 ). Integer networks [ 5 ] make probabilities identical across machines, as do our integer probability tables and portable kernels, and instance-adaptive compression [ 57 ] counts a per-image update in the rate, as we do.
blocks.zh: GPU上的经典格式已经解码:NVIDIA的库解码为JPEG 2000,HTJ2K [39],TIFF [38] 和通用格式 [37]. Huffman [61] 和 ANS [12,62,30,21] 相并分出部分或互分出 [14] 的流解码,矢量化的ANS将它带入已学习到的代码 [55]. 这些方法一旦知道许多值的概率,就与编码器平行;在一个已学习的编码器中,解码顺序决定了一次已知的数,而FMT的树使得它们成为一步的每一个值. 与矢量化的ANS一样,我们的车道保持分级状态,但车道编号遵循的是图像,而不是台阶,因此96至98,304个站台值的相通(第3.4节)。 整数网络 [5] 使概率在机器之间完全相同,我们的整数概率表和可移植内核也是如此,实例适应压缩 [57] 计算率中的每个图像更新,就像我们一样.

blocks.en: 3.1 A tree of pixels

blocks.en:
FMT decodes an image from coarse to fine, as Fig. 2 shows on a small grid. It first stores a sparse grid of pixels, the root : one pixel every S = 64 S=64 pixels in each direction, stored as is. It then adds the remaining pixels in L = 6 L=6 levels, each of which halves the spacing of the decoded grid.
A level sees the decoded pixels as the corners of squares and fills each square in two steps. First it adds the square’s centre , which has decoded pixels at its four diagonal corners. Then it adds the midpoint of each side, an edge , which now has decoded pixels on all four sides: the two corners of that side and the two centres next to it. The decoded pixels then form a grid twice as fine, which the next level fills in the same way, until every pixel is decoded. In coordinates, level ℓ \ell fills squares of side s = S / 2 ℓ − 1 s=S/2^{\ell-1} and adds the pixels at half that spacing, h = s / 2 h=s/2 : centres: ( y , x ) ≡ ( h , h ) ( mod s ) , \displaystyle(y,x)\equiv(h,h)\pmod{s}, edges: ( y , x ) ≡ ( 0 , h ) ​ or ​ ( h , 0 ) ( mod s ) . \displaystyle(y,x)\equiv(0,h)\text{ or }(h,0)\pmod{s}. (1) Each level adds three times as many pixels as were already decoded: in a 768 × 512 768\times 512 photo, the root holds 96 pixels, the first level adds 288 and the last 294,912. Two properties follow. Every new pixel has decoded neighbours on all sides, and the pixels added in one step never depend on each other, so a GPU can process them all at once ( Sec. 3.4 ). A neighbour that falls outside the image is reflected into it or replaced by the nearest decoded pixel, so the sides need not be multiples of 64. We call the structure a tree after the quadtree of its squares: every pixel is reached from the root through the levels above it, and its dependencies, on several coarser pixels, form a directed acyclic graph.

blocks.en: 3.2 Predict, then correct

blocks.en: Every new value v v is first predicted, as v ^ \hat{v} , from pixels decoded in earlier steps, and the file stores only the correction (residual) r = v − v ^ r=v-\hat{v} (Fig. S2). The finer the level, the closer the neighbours and the smaller the corrections. A correction is binarised into a short path of discrete decisions, as in Exp-Golomb codes [ 53 ] , JPEG’s magnitude categories [ 58 ] and JPEG XL’s hybrid integers [ 48 ] . The sign is folded in first, as in LOCO-I [ 60 ] : u = 2 ​ r u=2r if r ≥ 0 r\geq 0 and u = − 2 ​ r − 1 u=-2r-1 otherwise, so small corrections of either sign become small numbers. The first decision is the size of u u , its number of bits, cheap to code as small sizes dominate; the bits after its leading one follow. The modes differ in how they pay for these decisions ( Sec. 3.3 ): the fast mode stores them at fixed widths, the dense mode codes them with shared histograms, and the neural modes give every possible correction its own probability. Before coding, all modes but the fast one convert the colours with one of JPEG XL’s reversible transforms [ 48 ] , chosen by the sum of log 2 ⁡ ( 1 + | e | ) \log_{2}(1+|e|) over the residuals e e of LOCO-I’s predictor [ 60 ] .

blocks.en: An entropy coder turns each value into bits according to the probability the decoder will give it: a value of probability p p costs about − log 2 ⁡ p -\log_{2}p bits, so the better the probabilities, the smaller the file. The encoder and the decoder must therefore compute the same probabilities from what is already decoded. Classical codecs do this by counting: they sort values into a few contexts , classes of similar neighbourhoods, and code each value with the histogram of its context [ 63 , 60 ] . Learned codecs instead let a network compute the probability of every possible value from the neighbourhood [ 47 , 33 ] . Both hand their probabilities to an entropy coder such as rANS [ 12 ] , whose decoder keeps one integer state and reads each value by finding where that state falls in the value’s cumulative distribution. FMT offers both kinds, and a third that needs no probabilities at all ( Tab. 2 ). The tree fixes which values are decoded together; the modes decide how each value is predicted and how its path is paid for.
blocks.zh: 一个 en码器根据解码器给出的概率将每个值转换为比特:一个概率p成本的值大约为-log 2-⁡-\log_{2}p比特,所以概率越好,文件越小. 因此编码器和解码器必须从已经解码的东西中计算出相同的概率. 经典编解码器通过计数来做到这一点:它们将值排序为几个上下文,类相近的街区,并用其上下文的直方图来编码每个值[63,60]. 相反,学习的解码器让一个网络计算来自邻里的每一可能值的概率[47,33]. 双方将它们的概率交给一个像 rANS [12] 这样的等编码器,它的解码器保持了一整数状态并读取每个值,找出该状态在数值的累积分布中落到哪里. FMT提供两种,第三种则根本不需要概率(附件2)。 树固定了哪些值被解码在一起;模式决定每个值是如何预测的,如何支付路径.

blocks.en: The dense mode follows the classical recipe on the pixel tree. It predicts each new pixel by the rounded mean of its four nearest decoded neighbours ( Fig. 2 ) and codes the first decisions of each correction, its size and the bit after its leading one, with rANS under a histogram; the remaining bits, close to uniform, are coded at uniform probability. The histogram depends on a context made of two values: how much the four neighbours differ, and how large their corrections were, there and in the previous colour channel. Similar neighbourhoods have similar histograms in every image, so one codebook of 256 histograms, learned once on training photos, serves all images, and a file stores only which histogram each of its contexts uses. Decoding a value takes a few integer operations and no network. Its limit is the context: two hand-chosen values can tell only so many neighbourhoods apart.
blocks.zh: 稠密模式遵循了像素树上的古典配方. 它用四个最接近被解码的邻居的四舍五入平均值(图2)来预测每个新像素,并编码每个校正的首个决定,大小和前一个后的一个位,在直方图下为RANS;所剩的几位,相近于统一的,以统一概率来编码. 直方图取决于由两个值组成的上下文:四个相邻者差异有多大,以及他们的校正有多大,有的还有以前的彩道. 相似的街区在每个图像中都有相似的直方图,所以一个256个直方图的编码本,在训练相片上学习过一次,服务于所有图像,以及一个文件存储库,只有其每个上下文使用的直方图. 解码一个值需要几个整数操作,没有网络. 它的极限是上下文:两个亲手选择的值只能分辨出相隔如此多的街区.

blocks.en: The neural modes remove that limit by replacing the context and its histogram with a network that computes the probability of every possible correction from the neighbourhood itself. For each value, a small multilayer perceptron reads the nearest decoded pixels, relative to the mean of the nearest four, which remains the prediction; how much these four differ; and, in the second and third colour channels, the values already decoded at and around the same pixel. One-hot inputs tell it the level and the kind of step, so one network per colour channel serves the whole tree. It outputs a mixture of discretised logistics [ 47 ] , a smooth distribution over all corrections, which the encoder and the decoder turn into the same integer table for rANS ( Sec. 3.4 ). The network only prices each correction: a weaker one makes a larger file, never a wrong pixel. The networks are trained to minimise the code length of the corrections on crops of training photos. For more context, the neural modes split each step in two, so the second half also sees the first: the centres in two checkerboard halves, the edges as horizontal, then vertical midpoints.
blocks.zh: 神经模式取消了这个限制,将上下文及其直方图取而代之,取而代之的网络会计算出邻里本身每一次可能的校正概率. 对于每个值,一个小多层的能见度读取最接近的解码像素,相对于最近的四相的平均值,这仍然是预测;这四个相差多少;在第二和第三相色通道中,在同一像素上和周围已经解码的值. 单热输入告诉它等级和步骤的类型,所以每个彩色通道有一个网络服务整个树. 它输出出盘状物流的混合物[47],在所有校正中平稳地分布,编码器和解码器会变成同一种rANS的整数表(第3.4节)。 网络只给每个修正定价:一个更弱的让一个更大的文件,从不错误的像素. 培训这些网络,以尽量减少对培训照片作物的更正的代码长度。 对于更多的上下文,神经模式将每个步骤一分为二,所以后半部分也看到了第一个:两个检查板中的中枢分出一半,边缘为水平,再取出垂直中点.

blocks.en: A network trained on many photos is not the best one for a given photo. As JPEG XL learns a context tree for each image, the encoder of the neural modes adapts the network to the photo and stores the change in the file: a scale and a shift for each hidden neuron, the output biases, and a change of the output layer within a fixed random subspace (as in FiLM [ 40 ] and LoRA [ 19 ] ). A few hundred gradient steps minimise the photo’s code length plus a penalty standing in for the change’s coded size; the change is then rounded and entropy-coded, in a small share of the file ( Tab. 2 ). The decoder merges it into the weights once, so a tuned photo decodes as fast as an untuned one. The encoder also tries the best-ranked colour transforms and the 8 orientations, and keeps the smallest file (Sec. S4).
blocks.zh: 一个受过许多照片训练的网络对于给定照片来说并不是最好的网络. 随着JPEG XL为每个图像学习上下文树,神经模式的编码器会使网络适应相片并存储文件中的变化:每个隐藏神经元的尺度和变化,输出偏差,以及输出层在一个固定随机子空间内的改变(如FiLM [40]和LORA [19]). 几百个梯度步骤将相片的代码长度最小化, 加上对更改的编码大小的罚则; 更改后被四舍五入并编码为等码, 在文件的一小部分( Tab. 2 ) 。 解码器一度将它合并入重量中,因此调取的相片解码快于未调取的相片. 编码器还尝试了排名最好的颜色变换和8取向,并保留了最小的文件(Sec. S4).

blocks.en: When speed matters above all, the fast mode drops probabilities altogether: every correction is stored at a fixed width, so the decoder only reads bits. Instead of the pixel tree, it uses the tree of the reversible integer 5/3 wavelet of JPEG 2000 [ 7 , 52 ] , which, like the pixel tree, predicts new coefficients from coarser ones and keeps only the corrections. The corrections are stored in groups of 8 × 8 8\times 8 . Each group first stores, in one byte, the largest size among its corrections and the range of their sizes; each correction then stores how far its size lies below the largest, at the width that range implies, and its remaining bits follow. Since every field has a width known from its group’s byte, the decoder finds where each group and each correction begins with prefix sums, running totals that a GPU computes in parallel, and decodes all groups at once.
blocks.zh: 当速度最重要时,快模式会完全降低概率:每个校正都以固定宽度存储,因此解码器只读取比特. 取而代之的是像素树,它使用了可逆整数5/3波列的JPEG 2000 [7,52]的树,这与像素树一样,从相近的树上预测出新的系数,只保留了校正. 更正分为8×8 8\时组 8 (英语). 每组先以一字节存储其更正中最大大小和大小范围;再将每组更正的大小在最大大小以下,宽度所意味的宽度,剩余比特跟随. 由于每个字段都有从组的字节中得知的宽度,解码器会找到每个组和每个校正从前缀总和开始的地方,运行一个GPU并行计算的总和,同时解码所有组.

blocks.en: FMT decodes an image one step at a time, and everything inside a step in parallel ( Fig. 3 ).
blocks.zh: FMT逐一解码出一幅图像,并平行解码出一个步骤内的一切(图3.

blocks.en: Within a step, no value depends on another ( Sec. 3.1 ): a centre depends only on coarser pixels, an edge also on the centres of its level, the second half of a split step also on the first, and a later colour channel also on the earlier ones. The GPU therefore decodes a step in two phases: it predicts all its values and their probabilities at once, then decodes their corrections in parallel ( Fig. 3 b). With the three colour channels decoded in turn, a photo of any size takes 36 steps in the dense mode and 72 in the neural modes ( Fig. 3 a). This fixes the number of steps, not the time: a larger image has larger steps.
blocks.zh: 在一步之内,任何价值都不取决于另一步(第3.1节): a 中心仅依赖于相近像素,边缘也取决于其水平的中心,后半个相分步骤的后半部分也取决于第一个相分步骤,后一个相分色道也取决于前一个相分. 因此GPU解码分出分出两个阶段的一步:它一次预测其所有值及其概率,然后同时解码它们的校正(图3b). 由三个彩色通道依次解码后,任意大小相片在稠密模式下可走36步,在神经模式下可走72步(图3 a). 这固定了步骤的数量,而不是时间:一个更大的图像有更大的步骤.

blocks.en: An rANS decoder is sequential: it reads one value after another from its stream. To decode many values at once, the stream is interleaved: the values are dealt to many lanes , each a separate rANS decoder with its own state, run by one GPU thread [ 14 ] . FMT deals the values of every step to the lanes in turn, and each lane keeps its state from one step to the next. The number of lanes therefore follows the size of the image, not of the step: an image gets enough lanes that each decodes about T T values in all, a lane length that trades parallelism against the few bytes of each lane’s final state ( Tab. 2 ). Giving each step lanes of its own would need many times as many lanes for the same chain length, each with a final state to store, and make files 13% larger with our 16 × \times 2 (Sec. S3.3).

blocks.en: Lossless decoding needs the decoder to compute exactly the same probabilities as the encoder: a single difference in rounding makes it read a wrong value, and the error spreads to every value predicted from it. Floating-point results depend on the order of operations, which compilers, libraries and GPUs may change. We therefore turn each network’s mixture into an integer cumulative distribution, with fixed-point arithmetic and a table of the sigmoid, in which every value keeps a nonzero frequency (Sec. S5.1), and our kernels fix the order of every operation. The dense and fast modes compute with integers only, so any processor decodes their streams, and those of our small networks decode bit for bit on all three GPUs we tested.
blocks.zh: 无损失解码需要解码器来计算出与编码器完全相同的概率:四舍五入的一分一差使得它读取了错误的值,而误差会蔓延到从中预言的每个值. 浮点结果取决于操作顺序,编译器,库和GPU可能会改变. 因此,我们把每个网络的混合物变成一个整数的累积分布,有固定点算术和相模表,其中每个值都保持一个非零频率(Sec. S. 5.1),我们的内核确定每个操作的顺序。 密集而快的模式只用整数计算, 所以任何处理器都会解码他们的流, 而我们小网络的解码比特, 以比特方式在我们测试的所有三个GPU上.

blocks.en:
Two things decide how fast an image decodes and how small its file is: how many steps must run one after another, and how much of the decoded image each value can see. The tree trades a little of the second for much of the first
( Tab. 1 ).

blocks.en: In raster order, every value waits for the one before it; in the tree, only the steps wait for each other, and the lanes keep each decoder’s chain short. The lanes are not tied to the tree: any order that decodes groups of values could use them. What the tree adds is that these groups stay few and large for an image of any size, because its root is so sparse that storing it costs almost nothing.
blocks.zh: 按光栅顺序,每一个值都等它之前的一等;在树上,只有台阶相等,而道道使每个解码器的链条都短. 道不是被绑在树上:任何解码值组的顺序都可以使用. 这棵树所补充的是,这些组别对于任何大小的图像来说都很少,而且很大,因为其根部如此地稀疏而储存起来几乎一文不值.

blocks.en: Most pixels see more in the tree than in raster order: the three quarters of the pixels that the last level adds have decoded neighbours on all four sides, where raster order offers only those above and to the left. The price is paid at the coarse levels, whose decoded neighbours are far away: their values cost about twice the bits, but the first three levels hold under 2% of values. Against a wavefront, it costs small networks 0.3 to 2.4% of size ( Sec. 4.4 ).

blocks.en: To see what the tree costs, we train the same networks for a 2:1 wavefront, the most parallel order in which a value sees its left, upper and upper-right neighbours (Sec. S3.4). Our 16 × \times 2 and 64 × \times 2 then gain 1.6% on Kodak (files) and 2.4% (tuned code length), but the gain does not grow with capacity: a 512 × \times 4 trained both ways with a short recipe gains nothing once tuned. The wavefront, however, takes 78 times as many steps, a number that grows with the image: about 24,000 for a 4K frame, where the tree still takes 72 (our 16 × \times 2 decodes one in 33 ms, Sec. S3.4). Our kernels, built for a few large steps, decode the wavefront 40 × \times slower; a decoder built for small steps would narrow this gap, but synchronising its steps alone would take as long as our 16 × \times 2’s whole decode. Tiles stop the steps from growing, but not the cost of having many ( Fig. 5 , Sec. S3.4). Inside tiles of 64 pixels, the most parallel choice, the wavefront still takes 567 steps, 8 × \times the tree’s: with the same encoder and kernels, its 16 × \times 2 makes files 0.3% smaller than ours at 4.6 × \times the decode time (its 64 × \times 2: 0.8%, in tuned code length), and our 64 × \times 2 is 4.5% smaller in less than half that time. The tree thus trades 0.3 to 2.4% of size for 8 to 78 × \times fewer steps.

blocks.en: 5 Limitations
blocks.zh: 5 限制

blocks.en: FMT is built for 8-bit photos written once and read many times. Tuning to each photo takes seconds on the GPU, 3.5–8.9 s per Kodak photo with our 512 × \times 4 on an A100 ( HPAC-FT : 8.45 s [ 28 ] ) and 2–14 s per 2K photo with our fastest encoders (Sec. S4.4), and on a CPU, FMT is competitive only one image at a time. Our decoder keeps tables and buffers for each image size, 276–403 bytes per pixel, up to 9.6 GB for a 33-megapixel image (Sec. S7.1), or none if rebuilt per image (+1.5 ms, Sec. S7.3), and a 64 × 64 64\times 64 thumbnail still takes the 72 steps: 3.2 ms with our 16 × \times 2, against about 0.5 ms for CPU codecs (Sec. S4.5). The best codecs that adapt to each image remain 1.8–3.4% smaller on the full sets. Our 128 × \times 2 and larger networks have no CPU decoder yet, and their portable kernels cost time: 3.0–4.4 × \times in fp32, or up to 1.2 × \times with 8-bit layers (RTX 3090, 4090), for files at most 0.25% larger (Secs. S5.3–S5.4). Images of 10 to 16 bits (film masters, medical scans) need networks trained on them and wider frequency tables; we tested photographs only. Files need checksums: errors spread to finer levels.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: Our results suggest that much of the time learned lossless codecs take can go to sequential work rather than to their networks. A coarse-to-fine schedule designed with its entropy coder bounds this work, to a few dozen steps and a set number of values per lane, for an image of any size. On such trees, from a quarter of a millisecond to tens of milliseconds per photo, a codec without a network beats HTJ2K on both axes, small networks reach the file sizes of some learned codecs at classical speed, and our largest networks spend their decode mostly on arithmetic, not on entropy decoding.
blocks.zh: 我们的结果表明,学到的无损失解码器所花的时间大多可以进行相继的工作,而不是进入他们的网络。 一个粗细的到精细的进度表,用它的等效编码器设计,将这项工作绑定在几十个步骤和每道一组值上,用于任何大小的图像. 在这样的树上,每张照片从四分之一毫秒到几十毫秒,一个没有网络的编码器在两轴上都击败了HTJ2K,小网络以古典的速度达到一些已学习到的编码器的文件大小,而我们最大的网络则主要花在算术上,而不是用在解码上.

To separate what the order gives from what our networks, lanes and kernels give, we train our 16 × \times 2 again for two sequential orders, with the recipe of the main paper’s 16 × \times 2 (60,000 steps at a peak learning rate of 2 ⋅ 10 − 3 2\cdot 10^{-3} , then 120,000 at 10 − 3 10^{-3} , on the same crops) on the RTX 3090. In a 2:1 wavefront , step t t of a channel decodes every pixel with x + 2 ​ y = t x+2y=t , and each value can see every pixel with a smaller x + 2 ​ y x+2y : those to its left, those of the row above up to the one above and to its right, and more of the rows further up. No order in which every value sees its left, upper and upper-right neighbours has fewer steps. A landscape Kodak photo takes 5,367 of them, a portrait one 6,135. In raster order, every value is a step. Both orders keep the root grid and the order of the channels, and give each value the inputs it has in the tree, read from its 48 nearest neighbours decoded before it, with the inputs that name the level and the step held constant. Tab. S2 compares them with our 16 × \times 2 under one protocol: the ideal code length of each generic network, and after 300 steps of tuning its output layer to each photo; and, for the wavefront, real files from the paper’s encoder (top four colour transforms, 8 orientations, per-photo tuning, lanes of 2,048 values), decoded by the paper’s GPU decoder, whose kernels run a step of the wavefront as they run a step of the tree.
The sequential orders make files smaller, but by little: by 2.2–2.5% with the generic networks, 0.7–1.7% after tuning, and 1.6% in the wavefront’s real files, from 3.8% smaller to 1.1% larger per photo. A 64 × \times 2 trained for the wavefront gains more: 3.0% with the generic networks and 2.4% after tuning, against our 64 × \times 2 (3.3 and 2.8% after the first training cycle of both). The gap does not keep widening with capacity: a 128 × \times 2 trained for the wavefront with the recipe of our 128 × \times 2 gains 2.7% with the generic networks and 1.1% after tuning, and a 512 × \times 4, trained in both orders with one matched short recipe (30,000 steps from scratch on the RTX 3090, on the grid of DIV2K crops alone), 1.7% with the generic networks and nothing after tuning: tuned, the tree’s 512 × \times 4 is 0.5% smaller (2.713 against 2.726 bits per subpixel; Tab. S2 ): tuning to each photo saves 4.9% in the tree and 2.7% in the wavefront. A second training of the tree’s first cycle, with the recipe of the other orders, gives code lengths within 0.05% of our 16 × \times 2’s first cycle (3.087 and 2.955 against 3.086 and 2.954 bits per subpixel, generic and tuned), so the differences between the orders are not those between training runs. They pay about 3.0 bits for a value at every level, while the tree pays 5.6 at its first level and 3.6 at its fifth, but 2.82 at its last, which holds three quarters of the values ( Fig. S4 a).

blocks.en: The wavefront’s steps hold about 210 values each on average (220 in a landscape photo), against up to 98,304 in the tree. A Kodak photo takes 5,591 of them on average, 78 times as many as the tree (7 of the 24 streams are in a portrait orientation, which the encoder may choose for any photo), and their number grows with the image’s sides: about 24,000 for a 4K frame, where the tree still takes 72. With our lanes and kernels, which we built for a few large steps, the wavefront decodes 40 times slower: 258 instead of 6.5 ms ( Fig. S4 b), 46 μ \mu s per step; replaying the whole decode as one CUDA graph, which removes the launches from the host, still takes 235 against 5.2 ms. A decoder built for many small steps would pay far less per step. On the RTX 3090, a step without work costs 1.2 μ \mu s as a kernel in a CUDA graph and 0.76 μ \mu s as a grid-wide barrier in one persistent kernel, over 5,367 steps (0.09 μ \mu s as a barrier inside one block, on one multiprocessor). Synchronising the wavefront’s steps would thus take 4.1–6.2 ms for a landscape Kodak photo, as long as our 16 × \times 2’s whole decode, and 19–28 ms for a 4K frame, which our 16 × \times 2 decodes in 33 ms with our kernels; each step would also wait for the prediction and the rANS decoding of its values. Decoding the three channels as a pipeline, which both orders allow, would shorten the wavefront to about 1,800 steps and the tree to about 26. We have not built such a decoder, so the 40 × \times is that of our kernels, not a bound: for small networks, what the order gives is mainly a number of steps that does not grow with the image. With many photos in flight, the wavefront’s small steps could also fill the GPU at full load; what the tree keeps is a single photo’s time and the few photos needed to fill the GPU. Encoding takes about as long with either order (5.4 and 5.7 s per photo in this run, which did not cool the GPU as Tab. S10 does), and the per-photo update takes the same share of the file.

blocks.en: Width stops paying at the top of the family: our 768 × \times 4 makes files as large as the 512 × \times 4 on Kodak (2.589 bits per subpixel each) and only 0.1–0.2% smaller on the large photos (main paper, Tabs. 3 and 5), for 1.4–1.6 × \times its decode time. Both read the same inputs and are trained on the same crops, so at this size the data and the inputs, rather than the width, may bound the size of the files (the 768 × \times 4 is the 512 × \times 4 widened and trained for one more cycle, so the two are not fully separated); the 512 × \times 4 is the better trade-off, and we report the 768 × \times 4 to show where the family saturates with our training.

blocks.en: S4.1 Encoder choices

blocks.en: Tab. S4 adds the encoder’s choices of the main paper (Sec. 3.3) one at a time, without changing the networks: the colour transform its fast estimate ranks first, then the best of the top four, the best of 8 orientations, and finally per-photo tuning, whose update the file includes. Tuning gives most of the gain, and more so for larger networks: 3.7% for the 16 × \times 2, 4.8% for the 64 × \times 2 and 6.7% for the 512 × \times 4, against 0.3–0.7% for the colour transforms and orientations together. blocks.en: S4.3 Encoding time
blocks.zh: S4.3 编码时间

blocks.en: Tab. S10 gives the size and the encoding time with 200 and with 25 tuning iterations. The time covers the encoder’s choices, the tuning and the probabilities of every value; we time 8 photos, each after the GPU has cooled to 50 °C, so that the temperature limit of our machine never paused a timed encode. With 25 iterations instead of 200, files grow by 1.1% (16 × \times 2), 1.7% (64 × \times 2) and 3.4% (512 × \times 4), and encoding is 1.7, 1.9 and 3.4 × \times faster: 2.6–4.4 s instead of 4.5–14.9 s per photo. Without the cooling, the same encodes took 4.5, 4.9 and 22.2 s per photo, the 512 × \times 4 heating the GPU until our machine’s temperature guard paused it. On large photos, encoding takes several times longer: for the CLIC.p photos of the main paper, our encodes on the RTX 4090 took 32–51 s per photo on average, depending on the network. Tab. S7 shows where this time goes on the RTX 3090: tuning takes only 2.5–2.7 s for the 16 × \times 2 and 64 × \times 2 and 12 s for the 512 × \times 4 of their 29–46 s. Most of the rest went to three host-side parts of that encoder: the fast estimate that ranks the 42 colour transforms (11 s), the index tables of the photo’s two orientations’ sizes (8–9 s) and the choice of the update’s quantisation (4–6 s).

blocks.en: S4.4 A faster encoder
blocks.zh: 第4.4节 一个更快的编码器

blocks.en: Our faster encoder moves these parts to the GPU ( Tab. S6 ). A first version changes no byte: it ranks the colour transforms from residual histograms computed in one kernel (the same four best transforms for every photo), builds the index tables in one kernel ( Tab. S19 ) and copies all frequencies to the host at once. It writes the files of the main paper’s encoder byte for byte for every photo we tried: 24 Kodak photos with the 16 × \times 2 and 64 × \times 2 and 8 with the 512 × \times 4, untuned and tuned, and 4 large photos with the 16 × \times 2, 64 × \times 2 and 512 × \times 4, tuned; in 0.04–0.06 s per Kodak photo untuned with the small networks (first-ranked colour transform, identity orientation) instead of 1.3–1.4 s, and tuned in 10.5–12.2 s per large photo instead of 29–33 s. The 512 × \times 4’s long tuned encodes heat the RTX 3090 until our machine’s temperature guard pauses them, unless they start cold (as in Tab. S10 , which drops paused timings), so we time the 512 × \times 4 on the A100, and on the RTX 3090 only the pool encoder below, cooled to 45 °C before each encode, with none of its timed encodes paused. A second version also scores every candidate (colour transform, orientation and quantisation step of the update) by its exact code length under the decoder’s integer distributions, instead of the training-time estimate, and runs the 200 tuning steps as one captured CUDA graph, with the same loss, optimiser and learning-rate schedule. With the 16 × \times 2 and 64 × \times 2 its files are within 0.05% of the main paper’s, in 2.3–2.9 s per Kodak photo and 3.1–4.2 s per large photo (on an A100: 2.1 s per Kodak photo with the 16 × \times 2, 2.5–3.3 s per large photo). On the A100, the 512 × \times 4 takes 8.9 s per Kodak photo and 13–14 s per large photo (40–43 s with the main paper’s encoder), 87% and 59–61% of it in tuning. Tuned on a pool of 262,144 values whose features are computed once, in batches of 16,384 values instead of 65,536, it takes 3.5 s per Kodak photo and 7.2–7.8 s per large photo, with files 0.15% and 0.07–0.09% larger, and the 768 × \times 4 4.6 s per Kodak photo (0.11% larger); on the RTX 3090, the 512 × \times 4 takes 5.0 and 12.9–14.4 s, with files 0.14% and 0.05% larger, the 16 × \times 2 0.85 and 2.0 s and the 64 × \times 2 1.1 and 2.6 s, with files 0.01–0.16% larger. On large photos, 57–58% of its time on the A100 goes to the exact code lengths of its candidates, each a full pass of the 512 × \times 4 over the photo, and 31–32% to tuning (67% on Kodak). For comparison, on the A100, LC-FDNet takes 1.1 s to encode a Kodak photo and 8.0 s for a DIV2K photo, and ArIB-BPS 3.8 and 28.9 s.

blocks.en: Tab. S13 decodes on the RTX 3090, end to end as in the main paper, the streams that we encoded on the RTX 4090 (CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.8) for the main paper. The fast and dense modes and the 16 × \times 2 to 64 × \times 2 networks decode them bit for bit; the 128 × \times 2, 512 × \times 4 and 768 × \times 4, which run their layers as matrix multiplications in cuBLAS, do not: cuBLAS guarantees identical results only on GPUs of the same architecture and number of multiprocessors, with the same library version and while a single stream is active [ 36 ] , because it picks its algorithm for a matrix product, and with it the order of the sums, such as how the inner dimension is split between thread blocks, by the GPU. A second pair agrees as well: an A100 (CUDA 12.6, PyTorch 2.7.1), another chip than both (compute capability 8.0 against 8.6 and 8.9), writes the same untuned streams as the RTX 3090 (identity orientation, first-ranked colour transform), byte for byte, for every Kodak photo and each of the 16 × \times 2, 32 × \times 2 and 64 × \times 2, from the same models and code: the two GPUs compute every value’s probability alike, so each decodes the other’s streams. For the 128 × \times 2, 512 × \times 4 and 768 × \times 4, none of the 24 streams agree. These are two pairs of GPUs, each with the GPU and the software changed together, and our kernels for the small networks use the GPU’s approximate exponential, which other GPU generations need not compute alike; our 8-bit CPU networks use integer layers, a polynomial activation and an exponential of their own instead, which any processor that follows IEEE 754 computes alike. The fast and dense modes need no such care: their decoders compute with integers only, and our CPU and GPU decoders of the fast mode read the same files.

blocks.en: A variant of our kernels removes both causes ( Tab. S11 ). It replaces the approximate exponential, in the SiLU and in the mixture’s weights and scales, by one of its own (Cody–Waite reduction and a degree-6 polynomial in fused multiply–adds, within about one ulp) and the one logarithm, of an integer from 1 to 511, by a table; and it runs the layers of the 128 × \times 2 to 768 × \times 4 in fp32, in a kernel of its own in which every output is the bias plus the products summed in increasing order of the inner index, one fused multiply–add each, whatever the tiling. Every result is then defined by correctly rounded IEEE-754 operations in a fixed order. The encoder and the decoder both use these kernels, so the streams change, by at most 0.005% in size. The RTX 3090 and the A100 then write the same streams, byte for byte, for every Kodak photo and each of the six networks, the 128 × \times 2, 512 × \times 4 and 768 × \times 4 included, whose standard streams differ on every photo; each GPU decodes them exactly. On the A100, the 16 × \times 2 to 64 × \times 2 decode 3–5% slower, the 128 × \times 2 6% faster, and the 512 × \times 4 and 768 × \times 4, whose layers no longer run on the tensor cores, 3.0 and 4.4 × \times slower; on the RTX 3090, whose tensor cores are slower relative to its fp32 units, the 512 × \times 4 decodes 1.7 × \times slower. Our layer kernel reaches 17.7–18.2 of the A100’s 19.5 fp32 TFLOPS, so the loss is that of fp32 arithmetic against bf16 tensor cores: a layer of 512 neurons over 262,144 values takes 7.6 ms against 1.6 ms in cuBLAS (RTX 3090: 5.9 against 3.4 ms, at 23.3 of its 35.6 fp32 TFLOPS).

blocks.en: S5.4 Portable at tensor-core speed
blocks.zh: S5.4 以百分点速度移动

blocks.en: Sums of integers are exact in any order, so a product of 8-bit integer matrices gives the same bits on every GPU, whatever kernel computes it. We run the hidden layers of the 512 × \times 4 and 768 × \times 4 so, on the integer tensor cores ( Tab. S12 ), without retraining the networks: each row of activations entering a hidden layer is quantised to 8 bits with its own scale, its largest magnitude over 127, and each output channel of the weights likewise, once, on the host; the tensor cores sum the products in 32-bit integers, and one kernel per row converts the sums to fp32, scales them back, adds the bias and applies the portable SiLU, in correctly rounded IEEE-754 operations, then quantises the result for the next layer. A variant quantises each row over its range, with a zero point, since SiLU’s outputs reach only − 0.28 -0.28 below zero; its sums gain an exact integer correction. The first layer, whose inputs mix scales, and the head stay in the portable fp32 kernel. The RTX 3090 and the A100 write the same integer streams, byte for byte, for every Kodak photo, and each decodes them exactly. Quantising networks trained in floating point makes the files 0.11–0.16% larger with a zero point, 0.20–0.25% without; networks trained with 8-bit layers, as our CPU networks are, could lose less. Tuned to each photo, as are the streams of the main paper, the files would be 0.43 and 0.29% larger with a zero point if the update were tuned in floating point and quantised afterwards. Our encoder therefore tunes it through the integer layers: its forward pass computes them exactly, from rows quantised as the decoder quantises them, and passes the gradients straight through the rounding. The tuned files are then 0.25 and 0.21% larger on Kodak ( Tab. S12 ), 0.09 and 0.08% on CLIC.p/4 and 0.12 and 0.11% on DIV2K/4. On the RTX 3090, the integer kernels decode as fast as the standard ones: the 512 × \times 4 in 85.3 against 84.6 ms and the 768 × \times 4 in 125 against 130 ms, against 143 and 267 ms with the fp32 portable kernels. Tuned, on the RTX 3090, they decode a Kodak photo in 91.7 against 89.4 ms and 131.8 against 134.8 ms, the CLIC.p/4 photos in 429 against 442 ms and 622 against 721 ms, and the DIV2K/4 photos in 504 against 513 ms and 729 against 839 ms, every decode exact. An RTX 4090 decodes the 48 tuned integer streams of Kodak that the RTX 3090 wrote, all exactly, in 64.7 and 93.3 ms, against 53.6 and 76.9 ms with its standard kernels on streams it wrote itself (2.5884 and 2.5897 bits per subpixel, so the integer files are 0.25 and 0.21% larger there too): 1.2 × \times the time. On the A100, in one session, the 512 × \times 4 decodes in 89 ms against 81 and 168 ms, and the 768 × \times 4 in 127 against 86 and 312 ms; there the host limited the standard decodes: sampled every 100 ms, the GPU was busy 57 and 73% of their time, against 98% of the fp32 portable decodes’ and 75–76% of the integer ones’ (in the session of Tab. S11 , the standard decodes took 55 and 71 ms).

blocks.en: S6.5 Published times
blocks.zh: S6.5 公布时间

blocks.en: The published times of learned codecs in the main paper are those that HPAC’s authors measured on an RTX 4090D, with about 11% fewer multiprocessors than our RTX 4090, for every codec of their Tab. 3 [ 28 ] , except CALLIC ’s, which comes from its own paper (1.7 s per Kodak photo, its Tab. 2; the GPU is not stated) [ 27 ] . FNLIC’s paper gives 13 ms of “decoding inference” per Kodak photo on a GTX 1080 Ti, and its table times LC-FDNet at 0.61 s, against 1.71 s in HPAC’s measurement; in our runs, below, FNLIC’s whole decoder takes 0.53 s (0.52 s without deleting its temporary files, the time we compare) and LC-FDNet 1.0 s. We keep HPAC’s measurements for the codecs we did not run, the only ones that cover them all with one protocol. We found no public code for HPAC or CALLIC with which to time them under our protocol; DLPR, which we could run, took 3.8 × \times its published time, and ArIB-BPS, run on an A100 (below), 0.35 × \times .
blocks.zh: 主论文中已公布的已学习的解码器时间是HPAC的作者在RTX 4090D上测量的,其多处理器比我们的RTX 4090少了大约11%,除了CALLIC的自出自自自论文(可达克相片每分1.7秒,其分页2;GPU没有说明)[27]. 民解中心的论文在GTX 1080 Ti上给出了13毫秒的 " 解码推论 " ,其表格时间为LC-FDNet为0.61 s,而HPAC的测量为1.71 s;在我们下面的运行中,民解中心的全解码器需要0.53 s(0.52 s而不删除其临时文件,我们比较的时间)和LC-FDNet为1.0 s. 我们保留HPAC的测量数据, 我们没有发现HPAC或CALLIC的公用代码可以用来根据我们的协议进行计时;我们可以运行的DLPR占用了3.8 ×\时间它公布的时间,而ARIB-BPS运行在A100(低于),0.35×\时间上.

blocks.en: S6.6 FNLIC, LC-FDNet and ArIB-BPS on an A100
blocks.zh: S6.6 民解力量、LC-FDNet和ARIB-BPS关于A100

blocks.en: We ran them with their authors’ code and models on one A100-SXM4-40GB, beside our decoders ( Tab. S17 ), one photo at a time, from the compressed bytes to the pixels: for FNLIC and LC-FDNet the minimum of 3 rounds after a decode that we check against the photo (7 rounds for ours, as in the main paper). FNLIC fits latents and a small network to each photo, in 2 × 130,000 2\times 130{,}000 iterations; we took the fitted models its authors released, encoded them on the A100 with their encoder, and timed their decoder in its own environment (PyTorch 2.0.1, CUDA 11.7) from a bitstream file on a RAM disk. It takes 535 ms per photo, 450 ms of them in the 12 sub-image channels decoded one after another, each by computing a distribution for every value on the GPU, copying them to the host and decoding the channel there with torchac’s arithmetic coder (213 ms in all), and 17 ms in the shell commands it spawns to delete temporary files; without autograd it takes the same (536 ms). Even with a free arithmetic coder and without deleting files, it would take 304 ms, 24 × \times our tuned 64 × \times 2 there: most of its time goes to the 12 channels decoded one after another, each a round trip between the GPU and the host. The bitstreams its authors released, of the same size (2.881 bits per subpixel), decode wrongly on the A100, all 24, with 87–99.6% of the pixels wrong, as its documentation warns may happen on another device. LC-FDNet codes a quarter of the pixels with JPEG XL and the rest in 9 steps, each running its network twice on the GPU and torchac twice on the host. We follow its encoder and decoder scripts with its checkpoints trained on Flickr2K, with three changes that can only make it faster: the quarter goes through libjxl inside the process (lossless, effort 7, as its command-line tools at their default) instead of through PNG files, the streams stay in memory, and the GPU’s memory cache is not emptied between steps. It reaches 2.938 bits per subpixel (2.98 in HPAC’s table) in 997 ms per photo: 465 ms until the distributions reach the host, 220 ms in torchac and 30 ms in JPEG XL. ArIB-BPS codes the image bit plane by bit plane with a U-Net; with its released ImageNet64 models and its own evaluation (one round per photo: encode, decode and comparison, timed by CUDA events) it makes 2.781 bits per subpixel (2.78 in HPAC’s table), decodes every photo exactly in 3.59 s and encodes it in 3.78 s. Its network needs sides divisible by 16, so on DIV2K/4 we pad each photo on its bottom and right by edge replication, the padding’s bits counted; 10 of the 25 photos do not fit whole into the A100’s 40 GB, so we code them in two halves, each padded likewise. It then makes 2.516 bits per subpixel, 1.2% less than our 512 × \times 4 and 1.0% less than our 768 × \times 4, and decodes every photo exactly, in 25.9 s on average, 106 and 71 × \times their time. Our decoders are slower on the A100 than on the RTX 4090 with the small networks (16 × \times 2: 7.6 against 4.5 ms) and about as fast with the large ones (512 × \times 4: 58.7 against 53.5 ms).

LC-FDNet用JPEG XL编码了四分之一的像素,其余的则分9个步骤,每台在GPU上运行了2次网络,在主机上运行了2次火炬克. 我们用Flickr2K的检查点来跟踪它的编码和解码脚本, 有三个变化只能使它更快:季度通过进程内部的libjxl(在它们默认时作为它的指令行工具, 无所丧失, 努力7)而不是通过PNG文件, 它以每张照片997 ms(HPAC的表为2.98分)达到每个子像素的2.938比特:465 ms(直到发行到达主机),220 ms(火炬克)和30 ms(JPEG XL). blocks.en: S6.7 CPU codecs
blocks.zh: S6.7 CPU 编码器

blocks.en: The CPU codecs run under WSL2 on the i9-14900K, whose 8 performance and 16 efficiency cores give 32 threads. We do not pin threads to cores, but give each codec its best number of threads; pinning a single thread to any core gives the same time, as Windows moves it to a performance core.
blocks.zh: 在i9-14900K上运行于WSL2下的CPU编解码器,其8个性能和16个效率核心给出了32个线程. 我们不将线程钉入核心,而是给每个编码器最好的线程;将一线程钉入任何核心都会给予同样时间,随着Windows将其移动到一个性能核心.

blocks.en: S6.8 Two dense decoders
blocks.zh: 第6.8号 两个密集的解码器

blocks.en: The dense format has two GPU decoders, one built for a single photo and one for full load, each 1.2–1.5 × \times faster than the other in its own regime; we time each regime with its faster decoder.
blocks.zh: 密集格式有两个GPU解码器,一个为一幅相片所建,一个为满载所建,每张1.2–1.5×xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

blocks.en: S6.9 Reproducibility
blocks.zh: S6.9 可复制

blocks.en: We keep the logs of every measurement and recompute every reported number from them with one script. One CPU point, JPEG-LS on Kodak, is a re-measurement, since the session of its first measurement kept no output.
blocks.zh: 我们保存每个测量的日志 用一个脚本重新计算每个报告的数字 一个CPU点,即Kodak上的JPEG-LS,是重新测量,因为其第一次测量的会话没有输出.

blocks.en: S6.10 Newer versions of JPEG XL
blocks.zh: 第6.10号 JPEG XL 更新版本

blocks.en: Every JPEG XL number in the main paper and above is from libjxl 0.11.2, through imagecodecs 2026.3.6. libjxl 0.12 (July 2026) changed its lossless coding and its faster-decoding levels, so we measured again with libjxl 0.12.0, through imagecodecs 2026.11.11, and with libjxl 0.13.0 through its command-line tools: the same protocol on the same CPU, efforts 1 to 9, faster-decoding levels 0 to 4, every decode exact. The two versions write files of the same size. On Kodak, effort 9 makes files 2.0% smaller than 0.11.2 (2.828 against 2.885 bits per subpixel) and decodes them in 12.4 instead of 11.0 ms, so our tuned 64 × \times 2 is 0.4% smaller than it and 1.7 × \times faster; with faster decoding (level 1: 2.860 bits per subpixel, 8.5 ms) it is larger and still slower than our 64 × \times 2. On CLIC.p/4 and DIV2K/4, effort 9 makes files 1.1 and 1.3% larger than 0.11.2 (2.485 and 2.821 bits per subpixel), and on the full sets 0.9 and 1.0% larger (2.650 and 2.816). On all three sets, no setting of either version is both smaller and faster than any FMT mode; on Kodak, two settings join the frontier, between our dense mode and our 16 × \times 2: effort 9 at faster-decoding level 2 (3.032 bits per subpixel, 4.05 ms) and effort 3 at levels 2 and 3 (3.182 bits per subpixel, 3.3 ms), as effort 3 does in the main paper. Through libjxl’s own decoder, which keeps its threads from one decode to the next, the faster-decoding levels take up to 1.7 × \times less time on Kodak than through imagecodecs (effort 9, level 2: 2.42 ms), and the same holds. For decoding images into a training job, the comparison that matters is at full load, where JPEG XL leaves its images in host memory and takes the CPU’s cores from the rest of the input pipeline ( Sec. S9 ). We will report both versions in the main paper’s tables in its final version.

S9). 我们将在主要文件表格的最后版本中报告这两个版本。

blocks.en: S7 Memory, image sizes and host work
blocks.zh: S7 内存、图像大小和主机工作

blocks.en: S7.1 Memory
blocks.zh: S7.1 内存

blocks.en: Our decoder keeps, per image size, its index tables and the buffers of the size’s first decode, and reuses them for later images of that size. In the main paper’s runs, its parser also built the tables of our CPU decoder, which the GPU decoder does not read: 0.8 kB per pixel more, 1.1 kB in all for our 16 × \times 2 and 64 × \times 2, so that a 33-megapixel image needed 33.6 GB and spilled from the RTX 3090’s 24 GB into host memory. Our released parser (the light parse) takes from them only the number of root pixels; the streams, the kernels and the decode times do not change (30.6 against 30.7 ms for a 4K frame with our 16 × \times 2 on an A100). Our 16 × \times 2 and 64 × \times 2 then keep 276 bytes per pixel, 228 of them tables, and our 512 × \times 4, with lanes of 8,192 values and its layers in cuBLAS, 311–403 ( Tab. S18 ): a 33-megapixel image needs 8.5 GB with the small networks and 9.6 GB with the 512 × \times 4, and our 16 × \times 2 decodes it in 133 ms on the RTX 3090 instead of 725 ms with the unused CPU tables. Once these are in place, a decode of a Kodak photo by our 16 × \times 2 needs only 22 MB more. Every entry of the index tables is a function of the value’s index alone, which is how one GPU kernel builds them ( Sec. S7.2 ), so the decoding kernels could compute them on the fly instead, trading memory for index arithmetic in every step; we have not built that variant. The main paper’s encoder, untuned, needs 8.4, 15.2 and 27.0 GB at these sizes, with every network (GB: 2 30 2^{30} bytes). Our faster encoder ( Tab. S6 ) needs less, measured above the network’s weights on the RTX 3090, every stream decoded and checked: tuned, 1.1 GB for a Kodak photo with our 16 × \times 2 and 64 × \times 2 and 3.3 GB with our 512 × \times 4, 4.2 and 6.4 GB for a 2K photo (DIV2K 0801) and 12.4 and 13.6 GB for a 4K frame, 1.6–1.8 kB per pixel there; tuned on the pool, 2.1, 5.2 and 12.4 GB with each network; untuned, 875 bytes per pixel (512 × \times 4: 0.6, 2.9 and 6.9 GB). A 24 GB GPU thus tunes our networks to frames of up to 4K.

blocks.en: The tables that depend only on the image size, such as the positions of the values of each step and their neighbours, are built once per size and kept, and are not in the reported times. The decoder of the main paper’s runs builds them on the host, in 26 ms for Kodak’s sizes and 122–123 ms for a 2K photo with the RTX 3090’s host CPU ( Tab. S19 ), and its parser also builds the CPU decoder’s tables ( Sec. S7.1 ), 0.4 s for a Kodak photo and 4.3 s for a 2K photo. Every entry is a function of the value’s index alone, so one CUDA kernel, one thread per value, builds the same tables, which we check entry for entry on 13 sizes from 65 × 63 65\times 63 to 7680 × 4320 7680\times 4320 : in 1.9–3.4 ms for Kodak, 7.2 ms for 2K and 69 ms for 33 megapixels (1.8 s on the host). With it and the light parse, the first decode of a size, everything included, takes about 1 ms longer than a later one for a Kodak photo with our 16 × \times 2 (7.1–7.2 against 6.0–6.1 ms) and 5.7 ms longer for a 2K photo (19.6 against 13.9 ms), and 0.7–5.9 ms longer with our 64 × \times 2 and 512 × \times 4 ( Tab. S19 ); a process whose memory allocator has released its cache also allocates the tables and buffers again, 3.3–3.5 ms more for a Kodak photo and 19 ms for a 2K photo. A set of one size pays this once, and a set of many sizes once per size: the 11 CLIC.p photos of the main paper’s Tab. 3 have 8 sizes. The dense mode has no index tables, only staging buffers per image layout: on the same GPU, its first decode of a size, buffers included and without a CUDA graph, takes 1.1 ms longer than a later one for a Kodak photo (median over the 24 photos: 2.0 against 0.61 ms) and 3.2 ms longer for a CLIC.p or DIV2K/4 photo (4.8–5.0 against 1.7–1.8 ms); recording the graph that later decodes of the size replay adds 0.8–1.7 ms more.

blocks.en: To see what keeping tables per size costs when the size changes from one image to the next, we code the 5,000 photos of COCO val2017, JPEG photos decoded once to RGB, in 603 sizes (350 of them used once; 0.27 megapixels on average), with untuned streams, and decode them one at a time in the order of their file names on the RTX 3090 ( Tab. S20 ): with the tables of every size ready (each photo decoded once and checked, then three times after a short GPU warm-up, the fastest counted), with those of the 16 most recently used sizes kept, which a new size replaces 2,256 times, and with tables built for every photo. Keeping 16 sizes, in 0.9 GB, our 16 × \times 2 and 64 × \times 2 decode a photo in 7.2 and 12.4 ms, at most 1.0 and 1.4 ms more than with every size ready; building the tables for every photo adds 0.5 and 0.2 ms more. The dense mode needs nothing kept: decoding each photo without a CUDA graph, with staging buffers made for its stream, takes 0.80 ms, less than replaying the graphs recorded for each size (1.4 ms with every size ready), whose buffers must hold any stream of their size. On every fifth photo (1,000, encoded on the A100), our 64 × \times 2 makes files 0.9% larger than JPEG XL e9 untuned (the best of four colour transforms and eight orientations; 2.6% on Kodak) and, tuned to each photo, 1.0% smaller (95% bootstrap interval 0.9–1.2%), smaller on 672 of the 1,000.

blocks.en: S7.4 Host and GPU work
blocks.zh: S7.4 主机和GPU工作

blocks.en: HTJ2K’s decoder, nvJPEG2000, and our dense decoder both parse a stream on the host and decode it on the GPU. To see how much of a single-photo decode each spends on either side, we trace every kernel, copy and memset of the process with CUPTI while each decodes one photo at a time, on the RTX 3090 of our CPU machine, whose i9-14900K is a faster host than our server’s EPYC 7702 ( Tab. S21 ). Both keep the GPU busy for most of a decode: for 0.60 of HTJ2K’s 0.73 ms per Kodak photo and for 0.43 of the dense mode’s 0.54 ms, and for 73–75% and 81% of their times on the large photos (busy times from the traced runs, decode times from untraced ones: tracing slows the host’s calls, not the GPU’s work). The host’s share, the time in which the GPU waits, is thus 0.13–0.37 ms per photo for HTJ2K and 0.11–0.26 ms for the dense mode. Tracing adds 0.8–1.0 ms per photo to HTJ2K but only 0.04–0.06 ms to the dense mode, which replays one CUDA graph: nvJPEG2000 makes many more calls to the GPU driver. On this machine the dense mode is 1.1–1.4 × \times faster than HTJ2K in two sessions, with the files of the main paper; on our server, with a slower host and a faster GPU, it is 1.2–1.6 × \times faster (main paper, Tab. 3), and a profile on CLIC.p there shows the GPU working for about half of the dense mode’s 0.83 ms per photo (0.39 ms).

blocks.en: S10 Potential directions for further research
blocks.zh: S10 进一步研究的潜在方向

blocks.en: A video adds a time axis to the tree. In a frame predicted from the previous one, every level can also read the decoded pixels of the previous frame at and around the same position, so static and slowly moving regions cost almost nothing, while the number of steps per frame stays the same. Our measurements on large photos give an idea of the speed: one image at a time, the dense mode decodes a 2.4-megapixel photo, a little larger than a 1080p frame, in 0.83 ms, and the 64 × \times 2 network in 17 ms, about 60 frames per second; at full load, the dense mode decodes 7.9 gigapixels per second, as many pixels as 950 frames of 4K video per second. Lossless video is stored today with intra-frame codecs such as FFV1 [ 35 ] , decoded on the CPU. A tree that also predicts across time could bring learned compression to video masters, medical and scientific recordings and lossless streaming. Because the coarse levels come first, a stream whose lanes end with each level would also let a client show a frame before it has fully arrived, and drop its finest levels when the bandwidth falls short.
blocks.zh: 视频为树增加了时间轴. 在从上一个预测的帧中,每个关卡也可以在同一位置上和周围读取前一个帧的解码像素,因此静态和缓慢移动的区域几乎无所取用,而每个帧的步数保持不变. 我们对大相片的测量给出了速度的概念:一次一个图像,密集模式解码出一幅2.4-megapixel相片,比一幅1080p相框稍大一点,以0.83 ms为单位;64×\times 2网络以17 ms为单位,每秒约60帧;满载时,密集模式解码出每秒7.9千兆克,以多到950帧每秒4K相片. 无损失视频今天以FFV1 [35]等帧内编码器存储,在CPU上解码. 一种同样可以跨时间预测的树可以给视频大师带来有学识的压缩,医学和科学的录音以及无损失的流出. 因为粗细的关卡是先行的,一个以每个关卡为终点的行道会让一个客户端在完全到达之前显示一个帧,并在带宽不足时降低其最好的关卡.

blocks.en: Our encoder tunes a small update of its networks to each photo by gradient descent, the largest single stage of the 512 × \times 4’s encoding ( Sec. S4.4 ). A network trained to predict this update from the photo in one pass, a hypernetwork, would replace the iterations, as amortised inference replaces per-example optimisation elsewhere; the encoder would still keep the predicted update of a colour channel only where its exact code length shortens the file, as it does now, and could refine it with a few iterations.
blocks.zh: 我们的编码器按梯度下降来调整其网络对每张照片的微小更新,这是512×\times 4编码(Sec. 一个训练有素的网络,通过一个通道从照片中预测这一更新,一个超网络,将取代迭代,因为分期推论取代了其他地方的每个实例优化;编码器仍然只保留一个彩色通道的预测更新,只有当其准确的代码长度缩短了文件,就像现在那样,并且可以用几个迭代来完善.

blocks.en: To decode a pixel, a neural mode computes features of its decoded neighbourhood, so decoding also yields image features as a by-product. On CIFAR-10, whose 32 × 32 32\times 32 images make a tree of one root pixel and five levels, a linear classifier on the activations of our 512 × \times 4 predictor, with its bits and residuals, averaged per tree level and image quadrant, reaches 75.7% accuracy, against 62.3% for the same network with random weights and 41.8% for raw pixels; our 64 × \times 2 reaches 68.6% (with random weights, 60.6%). Training to compress thus adds 8–13 points over random features of the same size, in line with evidence that models trained to predict pixels learn useful representations [ 9 ] . Recognising images from a partly decoded stream, perhaps from its coarse levels alone, is a potential direction for further research.
